newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty edges up, 1-day depos ride higher.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty edges up, 1-day depos ride higher.

text.p: The Polish zloty closed a fraction higher against the basket of currencies after dull trade brightened up only by a brief afternoon dollar selling trend which lifted the local currency, dealers said.

They said foreign entry into Polish T-bills or a large importer order likely stengthened the zloty to three percent from parity on Monday, but said that any further gains would likely be capped by a central bank intervention.
"After a colourless day the zloty inched up on the back of late currency-selling which may have been linked to foreigner T-bill entry," said Mateusz Bieniek of Societe Generale.
The zloty closed at 3.05/3.00 percent from the trading band centre, stronger than Friday's close at 2.97/2.91 percent.
It was at 3.0815/30 to the dollar, up from 3.0840/55 on Friday and at 1.8230/40 to the mark, also up from 1.8235/50.

Dealers expected the zloty to remain within a band between 2.8 and 3.0 percent from parity for some time, adjusting mainly to dollar/mark changes on world markets as traders focused on the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meeting on Tuesday.
The market expected the zloty to stay flat against the basket even if the expected 25-basis-point interest rate rise occurs at tomorrow's FOMC meeting.
On the money market one-day rates continued to rise on Monday as banks squared reserve accounts before Friday -- the last working day of March's required reserve, dealers said.
Overnight rates closed at 22.85/23.10 percent, up from opening's 22.80/23.10 percent and tomorrow/next at 22.75/23.05, higher than Friday's 22.45/22.95.

At today's T-bill auction all minimum prices fell and the average yield of the benchmark 52-week paper rose to 21.43 percent as demand at the 1.2 billion zloty tender amounted only to 738 million. Foreign interest was minute, dealers said.
